Subsequent postoperative recovery was uneventful in these
patients. Unblinding criteria were not met at any point.
Three patients in the lidocaine group had mild
subcutaneous catheter site events. One patient developed
skin redness during the infusion, which resolved quickly after
the subcutaneous catheter was removed and resited.
Another patient was noted to have skin redness and swelling
at the end of the drug infusion. Oral antibiotics were
prescribed as discharge medication as a precaution, and
objective criteria for skin infection were not met. A further
patient reported mild pain at the subcutaneous catheter site
for 2 weeks after hospital discharge that resolved by the 30-
day follow-up. Of note, this patient dropped the infusion
pump during mobilisation on the postoperative ward,
leading to disconnection and early termination of study drug
delivery. Reports of other adverse events were infrequent
(< 5%) and none were classified as serious.
